+"""Test that pyreverse correctly handles Python type hints for UML generation."""
+
+import astroid
+from pylint.pyreverse.inspector import Linker, Project
+
+
+def test_type_hints_in_instance_attrs():
+    """Test that type hints are used to infer instance attribute types."""
+    # Create a temporary test module with type hints
+    test_code = """
+class C(object):
+    def __init__(self, a: str = None):
+        self.a = a
+"""
+    
+    # Parse the code using astroid
+    module = astroid.parse(test_code, module_name="test_module")
+    
+    # Create a project and linker
+    project = Project("test_project")
+    linker = Linker(project)
+    
+    # Visit the module to populate the project
+    linker.visit(module)
+    
+    # Get the class
+    klass = module["C"]
+    
+    # Check that instance_attrs_type exists and contains type information
+    assert hasattr(klass, "instance_attrs_type")
+    type_dict = klass.instance_attrs_type
+    
+    # The attribute 'a' should be in the type dictionary
+    assert "a" in type_dict
+    
+    # The type should be inferred from the type hint (str), not Uninferable
+    attr_type = type_dict["a"][0]
+    
+    # Check that the type is not Uninferable (which would be the case without type hint support)
+    assert attr_type is not astroid.Uninferable
+    
+    # Check that the type is correctly identified as str
+    assert hasattr(attr_type, "name") and attr_type.name == "str"

+from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
+
+
+def test_non_disjoint_cycles():
+    # Test that non-disjoint cycles are applied left-to-right
+    # [[0,1],[0,1]] should give identity: first swap 0,1 then swap them back
+    p = Permutation([[0, 1], [0, 1]])
+    assert p == Permutation([0, 1])
+    
+    # [[0,1],[1,2]] should apply [0,1] first, then [1,2]
+    # Start: 0->0, 1->1, 2->2
+    # After [0,1]: 0->1, 1->0, 2->2
+    # After [1,2]: 0->1, 1->2, 2->0
+    # So final: 0->1, 1->2, 2->0
+    p = Permutation([[0, 1], [1, 2]])
+    assert p.array_form == [1, 2, 0]
+    
+    # [[0,1,2],[0,1]] should apply [0,1,2] first, then [0,1]
+    # Start: 0->0, 1->1, 2->2
+    # After [0,1,2]: 0->1, 1->2, 2->0
+    # After [0,1]: 0->2, 1->1, 2->0
+    # So final: 0->2, 1->1, 2->0
+    p = Permutation([[0, 1, 2], [0, 1]])
+    assert p.array_form == [2, 1, 0]

+from io import StringIO

+
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'fixtures_regress'
+
+
+class AuthorManager(models.Manager):
+    def get_by_natural_key(self, name):
+        return self.get(name=name)
+
+
+Author.add_to_class('objects', AuthorManager())

+
+class Book(models.Model):
+    title = models.CharField(max_length=255)
+    author = models.ForeignKey(Author, models.CASCADE, related_name="books")
+
+    objects = models.Manager()
+
+    def natural_key(self):
+        return (self.title,) + self.author.natural_key()
+
+    natural_key.dependencies = ["fixtures_regress.Author"]

+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'fixtures_regress'
+        unique_together = [["title", "author"]]
+
+
+class BookManager(models.Manager):
+    def get_by_natural_key(self, title, author):
+        return self.get(title=title, author__name=author)
+
+
+Book.add_to_class('objects', BookManager())
+
+

+    INSTALLED_APPS=[
+        'fixtures_regress',
+    ]
+)
+class LoadDataNaturalKeysNonDefaultDbOtterTest(TestCase):

+    available_apps = ['fixtures_regress']

+        when natural keys use foreign keys.

+{
+ "model": "fixtures_regress.author",
+ "fields": {
+    "name": "JR Tolkien"
+ }
+},
+{
+ "model": "fixtures_regress.book",
+ "fields": {
+    "title": "The Ring",
+    "author": [

+    ]

+        # Load data into non-default database

+from datetime import datetime
+
+import pytz
+
+from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate, TruncTime
+from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
+from django.utils import timezone
+
+from ..models import DTModel
+
+
+class TruncTzinfoOtterTest(TestCase):
+    @override_settings(USE_TZ=True)
+    def test_trunc_date_with_tzinfo_parameter(self):
+        """
+        Test that TruncDate respects the tzinfo parameter when provided.
+        A datetime at 2015-06-15 23:30:00 UTC should be truncated to
+        2015-06-16 when using Australia/Melbourne timezone (UTC+10),
+        not 2015-06-15.
+        """
+        # Create a datetime that's late in the day UTC but would be next day in Melbourne
+        utc_datetime = datetime(2015, 6, 15, 23, 30, 0)
+        utc_datetime = timezone.make_aware(utc_datetime, timezone=pytz.UTC)
+        
+        DTModel.objects.create(
+            start_datetime=utc_datetime,
+            end_datetime=utc_datetime,
+            start_date=utc_datetime.date(),
+            end_date=utc_datetime.date(),
+            start_time=utc_datetime.time(),
+            end_time=utc_datetime.time(),
+        )
+        
+        melb = pytz.timezone('Australia/Melbourne')
+        
+        # When truncating to date with Melbourne timezone, should get June 16
+        result = DTModel.objects.annotate(
+            truncated_date=TruncDate('start_datetime', tzinfo=melb)
+        ).first()
+        
+        # In Melbourne timezone, 2015-06-15 23:30 UTC becomes 2015-06-16 09:30
+        expected_date = utc_datetime.astimezone(melb).date()
+        
+        self.assertEqual(result.truncated_date, expected_date)
+        self.assertEqual(result.truncated_date.day, 16)
+        
+    @override_settings(USE_TZ=True)
+    def test_trunc_time_with_tzinfo_parameter(self):
+        """
+        Test that TruncTime respects the tzinfo parameter when provided.
+        A datetime at 2015-06-15 23:30:00 UTC should be truncated to
+        09:30:00 time when using Australia/Melbourne timezone (UTC+10),
+        not 23:30:00.
+        """
+        # Create a datetime at 23:30 UTC which would be 09:30 next day in Melbourne
+        utc_datetime = datetime(2015, 6, 15, 23, 30, 0)
+        utc_datetime = timezone.make_aware(utc_datetime, timezone=pytz.UTC)
+        
+        DTModel.objects.create(
+            start_datetime=utc_datetime,
+            end_datetime=utc_datetime,
+            start_date=utc_datetime.date(),
+            end_date=utc_datetime.date(),
+            start_time=utc_datetime.time(),
+            end_time=utc_datetime.time(),
+        )
+        
+        melb = pytz.timezone('Australia/Melbourne')
+        
+        # When truncating to time with Melbourne timezone, should get 09:30:00
+        result = DTModel.objects.annotate(
+            truncated_time=TruncTime('start_datetime', tzinfo=melb)
+        ).first()
+        
+        # In Melbourne timezone, 2015-06-15 23:30 UTC becomes 2015-06-16 09:30
+        expected_time = utc_datetime.astimezone(melb).time()
+        
+        self.assertEqual(result.truncated_time, expected_time)
+        self.assertEqual(result.truncated_time.hour, 9)
+        self.assertEqual(result.truncated_time.minute, 30)

+import sys
+import pytest
+from _pytest.capture import EncodedFile
+from io import BytesIO
+
+
+def test_encodedfile_mode_should_not_include_binary():
+    """Test that EncodedFile.mode does not include 'b' (binary) flag.
+    
+    This test ensures that EncodedFile correctly reports its mode without the 'b' flag,
+    even when the underlying buffer has 'b' in its mode. This is important because
+    some libraries (like youtube-dl) check for 'b' in the mode to decide whether to
+    write bytes or str. EncodedFile only accepts str, so it should not advertise
+    binary mode.
+    """
+    # Create a BytesIO buffer (which has mode 'rb+')
+    tmpfile = BytesIO()
+    tmpfile.mode = 'rb+'
+    
+    # Create an EncodedFile wrapping the buffer
+    encoded_file = EncodedFile(tmpfile, encoding='utf-8')
+    
+    # The mode should not contain 'b' since EncodedFile only accepts str
+    assert 'b' not in encoded_file.mode, \
+        f"EncodedFile.mode should not contain 'b', but got: {encoded_file.mode}"
+    
+    # Verify that the EncodedFile can write str (not bytes)
+    encoded_file.write("test string")
+    
+    # Verify that writing bytes raises TypeError
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="write\\(\\) argument must be str"):
+        encoded_file.write(b"test bytes")

+from django.db import connection
+from django.db.migrations.executor import MigrationExecutor
+from django.db.migrations.recorder import MigrationRecorder
+from django.test import override_settings
+
+from .test_base import MigrationTestBase
+
+
+class SquashedMigrationUnapplyTests(MigrationTestBase):
+    """
+    Tests that unapplying a squashed migration marks the squashed migration
+    itself as unapplied when the replaced migrations are still present.
+    """
+
+    @override_settings(
+        MIGRATION_MODULES={
+            "migrations": "migrations.test_migrations_squashed",
+        }
+    )
+    def test_unapply_squashed_migration_marks_squashed_as_unapplied_OtterTest(self):
+        """
+        When unapplying a squashed migration with replaced migration files
+        still present, the squashed migration itself should be marked as
+        unapplied in addition to the replaced migrations.
+        """
+        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection)
+        recorder = MigrationRecorder(connection)
+        
+        # Manually record the squashed migration as applied
+        # (simulating it was applied in the past)
+        recorder.record_applied("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002")
+        
+        # Verify it's recorded in the database
+        applied_in_db = set(recorder.applied_migrations())
+        self.assertIn(("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002"), applied_in_db)
+        
+        # Now unapply the squashed migration by migrating to None
+        executor.migrate([("migrations", None)])
+        
+        # Check what's recorded in the database after unapplying
+        applied_in_db = set(recorder.applied_migrations())
+        
+        # The squashed migration itself should be marked as unapplied
+        # This is the key assertion - the bug was that the squashed migration
+        # was not being marked as unapplied, only the replaced migrations were
+        self.assertNotIn(("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002"), applied_in_db)
+        
+        # The replaced migrations should also be marked as unapplied
+        self.assertNotIn(("migrations", "0001_initial"), applied_in_db)
+        self.assertNotIn(("migrations", "0002_second"), applied_in_db)

+"""Test that decorated __init__ methods are properly documented."""

+import pytest
+from sphinx.testing.util import SphinxTestApp
+
+
+@pytest.mark.sphinx('html', testroot='ext-autodoc')
+def test_decorated_init_is_documented(app):
+    """Test that a decorated __init__ method shows up in documentation."""
+    # Create a test module with a decorated __init__
+    target_dir = app.srcdir / 'target'
+    target_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    
+    # Create a Python module with a class that has a decorated __init__
+    decorated_init_module = target_dir / 'decorated_init.py'
+    decorated_init_module.write_text('''
+from functools import wraps
+
+def my_decorator(func):
+    """A simple decorator."""
+    @wraps(func)
+    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+        return func(*args, **kwargs)
+    return wrapper
+
+class MyClass:
+    """A class with decorated __init__."""
+    
+    @my_decorator
+    def __init__(self, param):
+        """Initialize MyClass with param.
+        
+        :param param: A parameter for initialization.
+        """
+        self.param = param
+''')
+    
+    # Create an RST file that uses autoclass with the class
+    index_rst = app.srcdir / 'index.rst'
+    index_rst.write_text('''

+   :members:
+''')
+    
+    # Configure napoleon to include __init__ with doc
+    app.config.napoleon_include_init_with_doc = True
+    
+    # Build the documentation

+    
+    # Read the generated HTML

+    # Check that the __init__ method documentation is present
+    # The documentation should contain the __init__ docstring
+    assert 'Initialize MyClass with param' in content, \
+        "Decorated __init__ method documentation should be present in the output"
+    assert 'param' in content, \

+from django.contrib.admin import ModelAdmin, TabularInline
+from django.contrib.admin.sites import AdminSite
+from django.contrib.auth.models import User
+from django.test import RequestFactory, TestCase
+from .models import Author, Book, Holder
+
+
+class BookInline(TabularInline):
+    model = Book
+    extra = 1
+
+
+class HolderInline(TabularInline):
+    model = Holder
+    extra = 1
+
+
+class AuthorAdmin(ModelAdmin):
+    inlines = [BookInline, HolderInline]
+    
+    def get_inlines(self, request, obj=None):
+        """
+        Hook to dynamically determine inlines based on request or obj.
+        """
+        if obj is None:
+            # When adding a new author, only show BookInline
+            return [BookInline]
+        else:
+            # When editing an existing author, show both inlines
+            return [BookInline, HolderInline]
+
+
+class GetInlinesHookTest(TestCase):
+    def test_get_inlines_hook(self):
+        """
+        Test that get_inlines() hook is called and allows dynamic inline
+        configuration based on request and obj parameters.
+        """
+        site = AdminSite()
+        request_factory = RequestFactory()
+        request = request_factory.get('/')
+        request.user = User(username='testuser', is_staff=True, is_superuser=True)
+        
+        author_admin = AuthorAdmin(Author, site)
+        
+        # Test with obj=None (add view) - should only have BookInline
+        inline_instances_add = author_admin.get_inline_instances(request, obj=None)
+        self.assertEqual(len(inline_instances_add), 1)
+        self.assertIsInstance(inline_instances_add[0], BookInline)
+        
+        # Test with obj (change view) - should have both BookInline and HolderInline
+        author = Author.objects.create(name="Test Author")
+        inline_instances_change = author_admin.get_inline_instances(request, obj=author)
+        self.assertEqual(len(inline_instances_change), 2)
+        self.assertIsInstance(inline_instances_change[0], BookInline)
+        self.assertIsInstance(inline_instances_change[1], HolderInline)

+import numpy as np
+import xarray as xr
+from xarray.tests import assert_identical
+
+
+def test_coarsen_construct_preserves_non_dimensional_coords():
+    """Test that coarsen.construct preserves non-dimensional coordinates.
+    
+    This test ensures that coordinates that are not dimension coordinates
+    remain as coordinates after calling coarsen.construct, rather than
+    being demoted to data variables.
+    """
+    # Create a DataArray with a non-dimensional coordinate
+    da = xr.DataArray(np.arange(24), dims=["time"])
+    da = da.assign_coords(day=365 * da)
+    ds = da.to_dataset(name="T")
+    
+    # Verify initial state: 'day' should be a coordinate
+    assert "day" in ds.coords
+    assert "day" not in ds.data_vars
+    
+    # Apply coarsen.construct
+    result = ds.coarsen(time=12).construct(time=("year", "month"))
+    
+    # Check that 'day' is still a coordinate, not a data variable
+    assert "day" in result.coords, "Non-dimensional coordinate 'day' should remain a coordinate"
+    assert "day" not in result.data_vars, "Non-dimensional coordinate 'day' should not be demoted to a data variable"
+    
+    # Verify the shape is correct
+    assert result["day"].shape == (2, 12)
+    assert result["T"].shape == (2, 12)
+    
+    # Verify the values are correct
+    expected_day_values = (365 * np.arange(24)).reshape(2, 12)
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result["day"].values, expected_day_values)

+import pickle
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import matplotlib.figure as mfigure
+
+
+def test_pickle_preserves_dpi():
+    """
+    Test that unpickling a figure preserves its DPI value.
+    
+    This is a regression test for the bug where DPI was doubled
+    after unpickling on M1 Mac (and potentially other platforms).
+    """
+    # Create a figure with a specific DPI
+    original_dpi = 100.0
+    fig = plt.figure(dpi=original_dpi)
+    
+    # Pickle and unpickle the figure
+    pickled = pickle.dumps(fig)
+    fig_unpickled = pickle.loads(pickled)
+    
+    # The DPI should remain the same after unpickling
+    assert fig_unpickled.dpi == original_dpi, (
+        f"DPI changed after unpickling: expected {original_dpi}, "
+        f"got {fig_unpickled.dpi}"
+    )
+    
+    # Test multiple pickle/unpickle cycles to ensure DPI doesn't keep doubling
+    for i in range(3):
+        pickled = pickle.dumps(fig_unpickled)
+        fig_unpickled = pickle.loads(pickled)
+        assert fig_unpickled.dpi == original_dpi, (
+            f"DPI changed after unpickling cycle {i+1}: expected {original_dpi}, "
+            f"got {fig_unpickled.dpi}"
+        )

+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import xarray as xr
+from xarray.tests import assert_allclose
+
+
+def test_sum_min_count_multiple_dimensions():
+    """Test that sum with min_count works with multiple dimensions."""
+    # Create a simple DataArray with some NaN values
+    da = xr.DataArray([[1., 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]], dims=["dim_0", "dim_1"])
+    
+    # This should not raise an error
+    result = da.sum(["dim_0", "dim_1"], min_count=1)
+    
+    # Expected result: sum of all elements = 21
+    expected = xr.DataArray(21.0)
+    assert_allclose(result, expected)
+    
+    # Test with NaN values
+    da_with_nan = xr.DataArray([[1., np.nan, 3], [4, 5, np.nan]], dims=["dim_0", "dim_1"])
+    
+    # With min_count=1, should return sum of valid values
+    result_with_nan = da_with_nan.sum(["dim_0", "dim_1"], skipna=True, min_count=1)
+    expected_with_nan = xr.DataArray(13.0)  # 1 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 13
+    assert_allclose(result_with_nan, expected_with_nan)
+    
+    # With min_count higher than valid count, should return NaN
+    da_mostly_nan = xr.DataArray([[np.nan, np.nan, np.nan], [np.nan, np.nan, 1.]], dims=["dim_0", "dim_1"])
+    result_insufficient = da_mostly_nan.sum(["dim_0", "dim_1"], skipna=True, min_count=5)
+    assert np.isnan(result_insufficient.values)

+from django.db import models
+from django.test import TestCase
+
+
+class MultipleInheritanceBase(models.Model):
+    base_id = models.AutoField(primary_key=True)
+    field_base = models.IntegerField()
+    
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'model_inheritance_regress'
+
+
+class MultipleInheritanceOtherBase(models.Model):
+    otherbase_id = models.AutoField(primary_key=True)
+    field_otherbase = models.IntegerField()
+    
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'model_inheritance_regress'
+
+
+class MultipleInheritanceChild(MultipleInheritanceBase, MultipleInheritanceOtherBase):
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'model_inheritance_regress'
+
+
+class MultipleInheritanceUpdateOtterTest(TestCase):
+    def test_update_with_multiple_inheritance(self):
+        """
+        Test that queryset update works correctly with multiple inheritance.
+        Updates to Child model should only affect Child instances, not parent
+        OtherBase instances.
+        """
+        # Create some OtherBase instances
+        MultipleInheritanceOtherBase.objects.create(field_otherbase=100)
+        MultipleInheritanceOtherBase.objects.create(field_otherbase=101)
+        
+        # Create some Child instances
+        MultipleInheritanceChild.objects.create(field_base=0, field_otherbase=0)
+        MultipleInheritanceChild.objects.create(field_base=1, field_otherbase=1)

+        # Update Child instances
+        updated_count = MultipleInheritanceChild.objects.update(field_otherbase=55)

+        
+        # Check that Child instances were updated
+        child_values = list(MultipleInheritanceChild.objects.values_list('field_otherbase', flat=True))
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(child_values), [55, 55])
+        
+        # Check that OtherBase instances were NOT updated
+        otherbase_values = list(
+            MultipleInheritanceOtherBase.objects.filter(otherbase_id__in=[1, 2]).values_list('field_otherbase', flat=True)
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(otherbase_values), [100, 101])

+import numpy as np
+from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
+from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV
+from sklearn.svm import LinearSVC
+
+
+def test_refit_time_attribute():
+    """Test that refit_time_ attribute is set after fitting."""
+    svc = LinearSVC(random_state=0)
+
+    X = [[1, ], [2, ], [3, ], [4, ]]
+    y = [0, 1, 1, 0]
+
+    gs = GridSearchCV(svc, {'C': [0.1, 1]}, cv=2, refit=True)

+
+    # Test that refit_time_ is not set when refit=False

+        Content-Type based on the underlying file type, not the compression
+        extension.
+        """
+        test_tuples = (
+            (".html.br", "text/html", "br"),
+            (".html.Z", "text/html", "compress"),

+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+from sklearn.decomposition import SparseCoder
+
+
+def test_sparse_coder_max_iter_parameter():
+    """Test that SparseCoder exposes max_iter parameter for lasso_cd algorithm.
+    
+    This test ensures that the max_iter parameter can be passed to SparseCoder
+    and is properly used by the underlying Lasso estimator when using the
+    'lasso_cd' algorithm.
+    """
+    n_samples, n_features = 10, 8
+    n_components = 5
+    
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
+    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
+    dictionary = rng.randn(n_components, n_features)
+    dictionary /= np.sum(dictionary ** 2, axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]
+    
+    # Test that SparseCoder accepts transform_max_iter parameter
+    # and uses it for the lasso_cd algorithm
+    coder = SparseCoder(
+        dictionary=dictionary,
+        transform_algorithm='lasso_cd',
+        transform_alpha=0.001,
+        transform_max_iter=5000  # This parameter should be exposed
+    )
+    
+    # This should not raise an error and should use the specified max_iter
+    code = coder.transform(X)
+    
+    # Verify that the transform produces output
+    assert code.shape == (n_samples, n_components)
+    
+    # Verify that transform_max_iter is stored as an attribute
+    assert hasattr(coder, 'transform_max_iter')
+    assert coder.transform_max_iter == 5000

+

+class PostgreSQLPGPASSWORDOtterTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    """
+    Test that subprocess.run is used with PGPASSWORD environment variable
+    instead of creating a temporary .pgpass file.
+    """
+
+    def test_pgpassword_environment_variable(self):
+        """
+        Test that when a password is provided, it's passed via PGPASSWORD
+        environment variable using subprocess.run instead of PGPASSFILE.
+        """
+        dbinfo = {
+            'database': 'dbname',
+            'user': 'someuser',
+            'password': 'somepassword',
+            'host': 'somehost',
+            'port': '444',
+        }
+        
+        with mock.patch('subprocess.run') as mock_run, \
+             mock.patch('subprocess.check_call') as mock_check_call:
+            DatabaseClient.runshell_db(dbinfo)
+            
+            # Verify subprocess.run was called (not subprocess.check_call)
+            mock_run.assert_called_once()
+            mock_check_call.assert_not_called()
+            
+            # Get the call arguments
+            call_args = mock_run.call_args
+            
+            # Check that the command is correct
+            expected_args = ['psql', '-U', 'someuser', '-h', 'somehost', '-p', '444', 'dbname']
+            self.assertEqual(call_args[0][0], expected_args)

+            # Check that env parameter was passed with PGPASSWORD
+            self.assertIn('env', call_args[1])
+            env = call_args[1]['env']

+from sympy import symbols, expand, factor, I

+
+
+def test_factor_extension_drops_factor():
+    """Test that factor with extension=True doesn't drop factors.
+    
+    This is a regression test for issue #18895 where factor with
+    extension=[I] was dropping the (y-1) factor from (x-1)*(y-1).
+    """
+    x, y = symbols('x y')
+    
+    # Test case from the issue
+    z = expand((x - 1) * (y - 1))
+    
+    # Without extension, this should work correctly
+    assert factor(z) == (x - 1) * (y - 1)
+    
+    # With extension=[I], this should still preserve both factors
+    # This is the failing case in the issue
+    result = factor(z, extension=[I])
+    assert result == (x - 1) * (y - 1)
+    
+    # Also test with extension=I (not in a list)
+    result = factor(z, extension=I)
+    assert result == (x - 1) * (y - 1)

+from sympy import Symbol, latex
+from sympy.physics.secondquant import B, Bd, Commutator
+
+
+def test_latex_dagger_power():
+    """Test that LaTeX output for powers of dagger operators has correct syntax.
+    
+    The issue is that b^\dagger_{0}^{2} is invalid LaTeX (double superscript).
+    It should be {b^\dagger_{0}}^{2} instead.
+    """
+    a = Symbol('0')
+    expr = Bd(a)**2
+    
+    # Get the LaTeX representation
+    latex_output = latex(expr)
+    
+    # The correct LaTeX should wrap the base with dagger in braces before applying power
+    # It should NOT have the pattern ^\dagger_{...}^{power} (double superscript)
+    # It should have the pattern {b^\dagger_{...}}^{power}
+    
+    # Check that we don't have double superscript (invalid LaTeX)
+    assert r'^\dagger_{0}^{2}' not in latex_output, \
+        f"LaTeX output contains double superscript: {latex_output}"
+    
+    # Check that the output has proper braces around the dagger operator
+    assert r'{b^\dagger_{0}}^{2}' in latex_output, \
+        f"LaTeX output should contain {{b^\\dagger_{{0}}}}^{{2}}, got: {latex_output}"

+from django.forms.models import modelformset_factory
+from django.test import TestCase
+from .models import Author
+
+
+class CanCreateFormsetTests(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that model formsets can disallow new object creation using can_create parameter.
+    """
+
+    def test_can_create_false_disallows_new_objects(self):
+        """
+        Test that when can_create=False, formsets reject attempts to create new objects
+        even when extra forms are submitted via POST data.
+        """
+        # Create an existing author
+        author = Author.objects.create(name='Charles Baudelaire')
+        
+        # Create a formset with can_create=False
+        AuthorFormSet = modelformset_factory(
+            Author, 
+            fields="__all__", 
+            extra=0,
+            can_create=False
+        )
+        
+        # Simulate POST data that tries to add a new author
+        # by sending more forms than INITIAL_FORMS
+        data = {
+            'form-TOTAL_FORMS': '2',
+            'form-INITIAL_FORMS': '1',
+            'form-MAX_NUM_FORMS': '',
+            'form-0-id': str(author.id),
+            'form-0-name': 'Charles Baudelaire',
+            'form-1-name': 'Arthur Rimbaud',  # Attempting to create new author
+        }
+        
+        formset = AuthorFormSet(data=data, queryset=Author.objects.all())
+        
+        # The formset should be invalid when trying to create new objects
+        self.assertFalse(formset.is_valid())
+        
+        # Verify the error message indicates new objects are not allowed
+        self.assertIn('new objects are not allowed', str(formset.non_form_errors()).lower())
+        
+        # Verify no new author was created
+        self.assertEqual(Author.objects.count(), 1)
+        self.assertFalse(Author.objects.filter(name='Arthur Rimbaud').exists())

+import numpy as np
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+from numpy.testing import assert_array_equal
+
+
+def test_stackplot_twinx_dataLims():
+    """
+    Test that dataLims of ax1 are not replaced by inf when using twinx
+    with stackplot on ax1 and plot on ax2.
+    
+    This is a regression test for the bug where ax1.dataLim.intervaly
+    gets changed to [inf, -inf] after plotting on ax2 when ax1 contains
+    a stackplot.
+    """
+    df1_index = ['16 May', '17 May']
+    df1_values = [-22.717708333333402, 26.584999999999937]
+    df2_values = [-0.08501399999999998, -2.9833019999999966]
+
+    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots()
+    
+    # Create stackplot on ax1
+    ax1.stackplot(df1_index, df1_values)
+    
+    # Store the original dataLims of ax1 after stackplot
+    original_datalim_y = ax1.dataLim.intervaly.copy()
+    
+    # Create twinx
+    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
+    
+    # Plot on ax2
+    ax2.plot(df1_index, df2_values)
+    
+    # Get the dataLims of ax1 after plotting on ax2
+    final_datalim_y = ax1.dataLim.intervaly
+    
+    # Check that ax1's dataLims are not inf
+    assert not np.isinf(final_datalim_y[0]), \
+        f"ax1.dataLim.intervaly[0] should not be inf, got {final_datalim_y[0]}"
+    assert not np.isinf(final_datalim_y[1]), \
+        f"ax1.dataLim.intervaly[1] should not be -inf, got {final_datalim_y[1]}"
+    
+    # Check that ax1's dataLims remain unchanged (or at least reasonable)
+    assert_array_equal(final_datalim_y, original_datalim_y,
+                      err_msg="ax1 dataLims should not change after plotting on ax2")
+    
+    plt.close(fig)

+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+from matplotlib.contour import ContourSet
+from matplotlib.path import Path
+import numpy as np
+
+
+def test_contour_set_paths():
+    """Test that ContourSet.set_paths() method exists and works correctly."""
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
+    
+    # Create a simple contour set with filled contours
+    filled01 = [[[0, 0], [0, 4], [1, 3], [1, 2], [2, 0]]]
+    filled12 = [[[2, 0], [3, 0], [3, 2], [1, 3], [1, 2]]]
+    cs = ContourSet(ax, [0, 1, 2], [filled01, filled12], filled=True)
+    
+    # Get the original paths
+    original_paths = cs.get_paths()
+    num_original_paths = len(original_paths)
+    
+    # Create new transformed paths (simple translation for testing)
+    new_paths = []
+    for path in original_paths:
+        vertices = path.vertices.copy()
+        vertices += [10, 10]  # Translate by (10, 10)
+        new_paths.append(Path(vertices, path.codes))
+    
+    # Test that set_paths method exists and works
+    cs.set_paths(new_paths)
+    
+    # Verify the paths were updated
+    updated_paths = cs.get_paths()
+    assert len(updated_paths) == num_original_paths
+    
+    # Check that the paths have been transformed correctly
+    for i, path in enumerate(updated_paths):
+        expected_vertices = original_paths[i].vertices + [10, 10]
+        np.testing.assert_array_almost_equal(path.vertices, expected_vertices)

+from io import StringIO
+from django.core.management import call_command
+from django.db import connection
+from django.test import TestCase, skipUnlessDBFeature
+
+
+class InspectDBForeignKeyToFieldOtterTest(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that inspectdb correctly handles foreign keys that reference
+    a non-primary key field (to_field).
+    """
+
+    available_apps = []
+
+    @skipUnlessDBFeature('can_introspect_foreign_keys')
+    def test_foreign_key_to_non_primary_field(self):
+        """
+        Test that a foreign key referencing a non-primary key field
+        generates the correct to_field parameter in the model.
+        """
+        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
+            # Create the referenced table with a unique field
+            if connection.vendor == 'postgresql':
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_foo_fk_test ("
+                    "id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER UNIQUE"
+                    ")"
+                )
+                # Create the referencing table with FK to non-primary field
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_bar_fk_test ("
+                    "id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER, "
+                    "CONSTRAINT fk_other FOREIGN KEY(other_id) "
+                    "REFERENCES inspectdb_foo_fk_test(other_id)"
+                    ")"
+                )
+            elif connection.vendor == 'mysql':
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_foo_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER UNIQUE"
+                    ") ENGINE=InnoDB"
+                )
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_bar_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER, "
+                    "CONSTRAINT fk_other FOREIGN KEY(other_id) "
+                    "REFERENCES inspectdb_foo_fk_test(other_id)"
+                    ") ENGINE=InnoDB"
+                )
+            elif connection.vendor == 'sqlite':
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_foo_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER UNIQUE"
+                    ")"
+                )
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_bar_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER, "
+                    "FOREIGN KEY(other_id) "
+                    "REFERENCES inspectdb_foo_fk_test(other_id)"
+                    ")"
+                )
+            elif connection.vendor == 'oracle':
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_foo_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER UNIQUE"
+                    ")"
+                )
+                cursor.execute(
+                    "CREATE TABLE inspectdb_bar_fk_test ("
+                    "id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "
+                    "other_id INTEGER, "
+                    "CONSTRAINT fk_other FOREIGN KEY(other_id) "
+                    "REFERENCES inspectdb_foo_fk_test(other_id)"
+                    ")"
+                )
+
+        try:
+            out = StringIO()
+            call_command(
+                'inspectdb',
+                'inspectdb_bar_fk_test',
+                stdout=out
+            )
+            output = out.getvalue()
+            
+            # The foreign key should include to_field='other_id'
+            # since it references a non-primary key field
+            self.assertIn("to_field='other_id'", output)
+            
+        finally:
+            # Clean up the tables
+            with connection.cursor() as cursor:
+                cursor.execute("DROP TABLE inspectdb_bar_fk_test")
+                cursor.execute("DROP TABLE inspectdb_foo_fk_test")

+from django.forms import (
+    CharField, Form, MultiValueField, MultiWidget,
+)
+from django.test import SimpleTestCase
+
+
+class MF(MultiValueField):
+    widget = MultiWidget
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        fields = [
+            CharField(required=False),
+            CharField(required=True),
+        ]
+        widget = self.widget(widgets=[
+            f.widget
+            for f in fields
+        ], attrs={})
+        super(MF, self).__init__(
+            fields=fields,
+            widget=widget,
+            require_all_fields=False,
+            required=False,
+        )
+
+    def compress(self, value):
+        return []
+
+
+class F(Form):
+    mf = MF()
+
+
+class MultiValueFieldRequiredSubfieldOtterTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    def test_multivaluefield_respects_required_subfield(self):
+        """
+        Test that MultiValueField with require_all_fields=False and required=False
+        still validates required subfields. When a required subfield is empty,
+        the form should be invalid.
+        """
+        f = F({
+            'mf_0': '',
+            'mf_1': '',
+        })
+        # This should be False because mf_1 corresponds to a required CharField
+        self.assertFalse(f.is_valid())

+from django.contrib import admin
+from django.contrib.admin import ModelAdmin, site
+from django.contrib.auth.models import User
+from django.test import RequestFactory, TestCase
+
+from .models import Book, Department, Employee
+
+
+class RelatedFieldOrderingOtterTest(TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpTestData(cls):
+        cls.dept_it = Department.objects.create(code='IT', description='IT Department')
+        cls.dept_sales = Department.objects.create(code='Sales', description='Sales Department')
+        cls.dept_hr = Department.objects.create(code='HR', description='HR Department')
+        
+        cls.charlie = Employee.objects.create(name='charlie', department=cls.dept_hr)
+        cls.bob = Employee.objects.create(name='bob', department=cls.dept_sales)
+        cls.alfred = Employee.objects.create(name='alfred', department=cls.dept_it)
+        
+        # Create books with all employees so they all appear in the filter
+        Book.objects.create(title='Book 1', employee=cls.bob)
+        Book.objects.create(title='Book 2', employee=cls.charlie)
+        Book.objects.create(title='Book 3', employee=cls.alfred)
+        
+        cls.user = User.objects.create_superuser(username='admin', password='pass', email='admin@test.com')
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.request_factory = RequestFactory()
+
+    def test_relatedfieldlistfilter_fallback_to_model_meta_ordering(self):
+        """
+        RelatedFieldListFilter should fall back to Model._meta.ordering
+        when no ModelAdmin ordering is defined.
+        """
+        # Employee model has Meta.ordering = ('name',)
+        # We don't register EmployeeAdmin with custom ordering
+        
+        class BookAdmin(ModelAdmin):
+            list_filter = ('employee',)
+
+        modeladmin = BookAdmin(Book, site)
+        request = self.request_factory.get('/')
+        request.user = self.user
+        changelist = modeladmin.get_changelist_instance(request)
+        filterspec = changelist.get_filters(request)[0][0]
+        
+        # Should be ordered by name (Model._meta.ordering) since no ModelAdmin ordering exists
+        # All three employees should appear in alphabetical order by name
+        choices = list(filterspec.lookup_choices)
+        expected = [(self.alfred.pk, 'alfred'), (self.bob.pk, 'bob'), (self.charlie.pk, 'charlie')]
+        self.assertEqual(choices, expected)

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+import numpy as np
+from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegressionCV, LogisticRegression
+from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
+from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
+
+
+def test_logistic_regression_cv_multinomial_scorer():
+    """Test that LogisticRegressionCV with multi_class='multinomial' 
+    uses multinomial (softmax) probabilities for scoring, not OvR probabilities.
+    
+    This test verifies the fix for issue #8720 where probabilistic scorers
+    like neg_log_loss were incorrectly using OvR approach instead of 
+    multinomial approach when multi_class='multinomial' was specified.
+    """
+    # Create a simple multiclass classification dataset
+    np.random.seed(42)
+    X, y = make_classification(n_samples=200, n_features=5, n_informative=3,
+                               n_redundant=0, n_classes=3, n_clusters_per_class=1,
+                               random_state=42)
+    
+    # Fit LogisticRegressionCV with multinomial and neg_log_loss scorer
+    lr_cv = LogisticRegressionCV(
+        Cs=[1.0],
+        cv=2,
+        scoring='neg_log_loss',
+        multi_class='multinomial',
+        solver='lbfgs',
+        random_state=42,
+        max_iter=1000
+    )
+    lr_cv.fit(X, y)
+    
+    # Fit a regular LogisticRegression with multinomial to compare
+    lr_multi = LogisticRegression(
+        C=1.0,
+        multi_class='multinomial',
+        solver='lbfgs',
+        random_state=42,
+        max_iter=1000
+    )
+    lr_multi.fit(X, y)
+    
+    # Fit a regular LogisticRegression with ovr to compare
+    lr_ovr = LogisticRegression(
+        C=1.0,
+        multi_class='ovr',
+        solver='lbfgs',
+        random_state=42,
+        max_iter=1000
+    )
+    lr_ovr.fit(X, y)
+    
+    # Get predictions from both models
+    proba_cv = lr_cv.predict_proba(X)
+    proba_multi = lr_multi.predict_proba(X)
+    proba_ovr = lr_ovr.predict_proba(X)
+    
+    # Calculate log loss for each
+    loss_cv = -log_loss(y, proba_cv)
+    loss_multi = -log_loss(y, proba_multi)
+    loss_ovr = -log_loss(y, proba_ovr)
+    
+    # The CV score should be closer to multinomial than to OvR
+    # because it should use multinomial approach for scoring
+    diff_to_multi = abs(lr_cv.scores_[1].mean() - loss_multi)
+    diff_to_ovr = abs(lr_cv.scores_[1].mean() - loss_ovr)
+    
+    # This assertion will fail before the fix (when OvR is incorrectly used)
+    # and pass after the fix (when multinomial is correctly used)
+    assert diff_to_multi < diff_to_ovr, (
+        "LogisticRegressionCV with multi_class='multinomial' should use "
+        "multinomial probabilities for scoring, not OvR probabilities. "
+        f"Difference to multinomial: {diff_to_multi}, "
+        f"Difference to OvR: {diff_to_ovr}"
+    )

+from sympy.parsing.sympy_parser import parse_expr
+from sympy.core.relational import Lt, Le, Gt, Ge, Eq, Ne
+from sympy.core.numbers import Integer
+
+
+def test_parse_expr_evaluate_false_relational():
+    """Test that evaluate=False parameter is respected for relational expressions."""
+    # Test Lt (less than)
+    result = parse_expr('1 < 2', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Lt(1, 2, evaluate=False)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert str(result) == '1 < 2'
+    assert result != True  # Should not evaluate to True
+    
+    # Test Le (less than or equal)
+    result = parse_expr('1 <= 2', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Le(1, 2, evaluate=False)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert str(result) == '1 <= 2'
+    
+    # Test Gt (greater than)
+    result = parse_expr('2 > 1', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Gt(2, 1, evaluate=False)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert str(result) == '2 > 1'
+    
+    # Test Ge (greater than or equal)
+    result = parse_expr('2 >= 1', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Ge(2, 1, evaluate=False)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert str(result) == '2 >= 1'
+    
+    # Test Eq (equality)
+    result = parse_expr('1 == 1', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Eq(1, 1, evaluate=False)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert str(result) == 'Eq(1, 1)'
+    
+    # Test Ne (not equal)
+    result = parse_expr('1 != 2', evaluate=False)
+    expected = Ne(1, 2, evaluate=False)

+from django.contrib.admin import ModelAdmin
+from django.contrib.admin.sites import AdminSite
+from django.core import checks
+from django.db import models
+from django.test import SimpleTestCase
+from django.test.utils import isolate_apps
+
+
+class DescriptorField:
+    """
+    A field descriptor that mimics django-positions PositionField behavior.
+    It raises AttributeError when accessed on the model class (not instance).
+    """
+    def __init__(self, name):
+        self.name = name
+    
+    def __get__(self, instance, owner):
+        if instance is None:
+            # Accessed on class, not instance - raise AttributeError
+            # This mimics the behavior of PositionField
+            raise AttributeError(f"'{owner.__name__}' object has no attribute '{self.name}'")
+        return getattr(instance, f'_{self.name}', 0)
+    
+    def __set__(self, instance, value):
+        setattr(instance, f'_{self.name}', value)
+
+
+@isolate_apps('admin_checks')
+class ListDisplayDescriptorFieldTests(SimpleTestCase):
+    """
+    Test that fields accessible only via instance (descriptors that raise
+    AttributeError on class access) don't incorrectly trigger admin.E108.
+    """
+    
+    def test_list_display_with_descriptor_field_accessible_only_via_instance(self):
+        """
+        Test that a field which is a descriptor that raises AttributeError
+        when accessed on the model class (but works on instances) should not
+        raise admin.E108 if it's a valid model field.
+        """
+        class TestModel(models.Model):
+            name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
+            order = models.IntegerField(default=0)
+            
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'admin_checks'
+        
+        # Add a descriptor that mimics PositionField behavior
+        TestModel.order = DescriptorField('order')
+        
+        # Add the field to _meta so get_field() can find it
+        order_field = models.IntegerField(default=0)
+        order_field.set_attributes_from_name('order')
+        TestModel._meta.local_fields.append(order_field)
+        
+        class TestModelAdmin(ModelAdmin):
+            list_display = ['name', 'order']
+        
+        # This should not raise any errors
+        # The 'order' field exists in _meta even though hasattr(TestModel, 'order') 
+        # raises AttributeError
+        errors = TestModelAdmin(TestModel, AdminSite()).check()
+        
+        # Should return empty list (no errors)
+        self.assertEqual(errors, [])

+from django.db import models
+from django.test import SimpleTestCase
+from django.db.migrations.state import ProjectState, ModelState
+
+
+class MixedCaseAppNameForeignKeyTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    """
+    Test that ForeignKey fields work correctly with mixed-case app names.
+    This tests the issue where makemigrations crashes for ForeignKey with
+    mixed-case app name like 'DJ_RegLogin'.
+    """
+    
+    def test_foreign_key_with_mixed_case_app_name(self):
+        """
+        Test that a ForeignKey can reference a model in the same app
+        when the app name has mixed case (e.g., 'DJ_RegLogin').
+        
+        This should not raise a ValueError about the app not being installed
+        when the lazy reference is resolved.
+        """
+        # Create a ProjectState with models that have mixed-case app name
+        project_state = ProjectState()
+        
+        # Add Category model
+        project_state.add_model(ModelState(
+            app_label='DJ_RegLogin',
+            name='Category',
+            fields=[
+                ('id', models.AutoField(primary_key=True)),
+                ('title', models.CharField(max_length=100)),
+            ],
+        ))
+        
+        # Add Content model with ForeignKey to Category
+        project_state.add_model(ModelState(
+            app_label='DJ_RegLogin',
+            name='Content',
+            fields=[
+                ('id', models.AutoField(primary_key=True)),
+                ('title', models.CharField(max_length=100)),
+                ('category', models.ForeignKey('DJ_RegLogin.Category', on_delete=models.CASCADE)),
+            ],
+        ))
+        
+        # Render the models - this should not raise ValueError
+        # about 'dj_reglogin' app not being installed
+        try:
+            rendered_apps = project_state.apps
+            rendered_models = list(rendered_apps.get_models())
+            # If we get here without exception, the test passes
+            # Verify that both models are present
+            model_labels = {model._meta.label_lower for model in rendered_models}
+            self.assertIn('dj_reglogin.category', model_labels)
+            self.assertIn('dj_reglogin.content', model_labels)
+        except ValueError as e:
+            if "isn't installed" in str(e):
+                self.fail(f"ForeignKey resolution failed with mixed-case app name: {e}")
+            raise

+import numpy as np
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+from numpy.testing import assert_allclose
+
+
+def test_inverted_log_scale_limits():
+    """
+    Test that setting inverted limits works for log scale axes.
+    
+    This is a regression test for the issue where inverting a log axis
+    using its limits (e.g., ax.set_ylim(max, min)) does not work in
+    matplotlib 3.1.0+.
+    """
+    # Test with y-axis
+    y = np.linspace(1000e2, 1, 100)
+    x = np.exp(-np.linspace(0, 1, y.size))
+    
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
+    ax.plot(x, y)
+    ax.set_yscale('log')
+    ax.set_ylim(y.max(), y.min())
+    
+    bottom, top = ax.get_ylim()
+    # When inverted, bottom should be greater than top
+    assert bottom > top, f"Expected inverted y-axis with bottom > top, got bottom={bottom}, top={top}"
+    assert_allclose(bottom, y.max(), rtol=0.1)
+    assert_allclose(top, y.min(), rtol=0.1)
+    plt.close(fig)
+    
+    # Test with x-axis
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
+    ax.plot(y, x)
+    ax.set_xscale('log')
+    ax.set_xlim(y.max(), y.min())
+    
+    left, right = ax.get_xlim()
+    # When inverted, left should be greater than right
+    assert left > right, f"Expected inverted x-axis with left > right, got left={left}, right={right}"
+    assert_allclose(left, y.max(), rtol=0.1)
+    assert_allclose(right, y.min(), rtol=0.1)
+    plt.close(fig)

+from io import StringIO
+from unittest import mock
+
+from django.core.management import call_command
+from django.db import connection, models
+from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
+from django.test.utils import isolate_apps
+
+
+class StrictRouter:
+    """
+    A router that validates that allow_migrate is called with correct
+    (app_label, model_name) pairs - i.e., the model should actually
+    belong to the app_label.
+    """
+    def allow_migrate(self, db, app_label, model_name=None, **hints):
+        # If model_name is provided, verify it belongs to the app_label
+        if model_name is not None:
+            model = hints.get('model')
+            if model is not None:
+                # The model's app_label should match the app_label parameter
+                if model._meta.app_label != app_label:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"Router received incorrect pair: app_label={app_label}, "
+                        f"model_name={model_name}, but model's actual app_label="
+                        f"{model._meta.app_label}"
+                    )
+        return True
+
+
+class MakeMigrationsRouterOtterTest(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that makemigrations calls allow_migrate() with correct
+    (app_label, model_name) pairs during consistency checks.
+    """
+
+    @isolate_apps('migrations', 'auth')
+    @override_settings(
+        DATABASE_ROUTERS=['tests.migrations.test_makemigrations_router_otter_test.StrictRouter'],
+        MIGRATION_MODULES={'migrations': 'migrations.test_migrations', 'auth': 'migrations.test_migrations_auth'}
+    )
+    def test_makemigrations_router_allow_migrate_correct_pairs(self):
+        """
+        Test that makemigrations consistency check calls allow_migrate()
+        with correct (app_label, model) pairs - each model should be
+        checked with its own app_label, not with other app_labels.
+        """
+        # Create a model in the migrations app
+        class TestModel(models.Model):
+            name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
+            
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'migrations'
+        
+        out = StringIO()
+        
+        # This should not raise ValueError from StrictRouter
+        # The bug would cause allow_migrate to be called with incorrect pairs
+        # like (app_label='auth', model=TestModel) where TestModel.app_label='migrations'
+        try:
+            call_command('makemigrations', 'migrations', '--dry-run', stdout=out, verbosity=0)
+        except ValueError as e:
+            if "Router received incorrect pair" in str(e):
+                self.fail(f"makemigrations called allow_migrate with incorrect app_label/model pair: {e}")
+            raise

+import numpy as np
+from numpy.testing import assert_array_equal
+from astropy.nddata import NDDataRef
+
+
+def test_mask_propagation_with_missing_mask_bitwise_or():
+    """
+    Test that mask propagation with np.bitwise_or works when one operand
+    has no mask. This is a regression test for issue where NDDataRef mask
+    propagation fails in v5.3 when one operand does not have a mask.
+    """
+    array = np.array([[0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0]])
+    mask = np.array([[0, 1, 64], [8, 0, 1], [2, 1, 0]])
+
+    nref_nomask = NDDataRef(array)
+    nref_mask = NDDataRef(array, mask=mask)
+
+    # Test: multiply mask by constant (mask * no mask)
+    # This should not raise TypeError
+    result1 = nref_mask.multiply(1., handle_mask=np.bitwise_or)
+    assert_array_equal(result1.mask, mask)
+
+    # Test: multiply mask by no mask (mask * no mask)
+    # This should not raise TypeError
+    result2 = nref_mask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or)
+    assert_array_equal(result2.mask, mask)
+
+    # Test: multiply no mask by mask (no mask * mask)
+    # This should not raise TypeError
+    result3 = nref_nomask.multiply(nref_mask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or)
+    assert_array_equal(result3.mask, mask)

+from django.contrib.auth.models import User
+from django.db.models import OuterRef, Subquery
+from django.test import TestCase
+from django.utils.functional import SimpleLazyObject
+
+from .models import Author, Book, Publisher
+
+
+class SimpleLazyObjectSubqueryTestOtterTest(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that SimpleLazyObject works with nested subquery annotations.
+    This is a regression test for the issue where SimpleLazyObject fails
+    when used in a queryset filter with nested subquery annotations.
+    """
+
+    def test_simplelazyobject_with_nested_subquery_annotation(self):
+        """
+        Test that SimpleLazyObject can be used in a filter with nested subquery annotations.
+        """
+        # Create a user
+        user = User.objects.create_user("testuser")
+        
+        # Create test data
+        publisher = Publisher.objects.create(name="Test Publisher", num_awards=5)
+        author = Author.objects.create(name="Test Author", age=30)
+        book = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn="1234567890",
+            name="Test Book",
+            pages=100,
+            rating=4.5,
+            price=10.0,
+            contact=author,
+            publisher=publisher,
+            pubdate="2023-01-01"
+        )
+        book.authors.add(author)
+        
+        # Create another publisher and book with the user as contact
+        publisher2 = Publisher.objects.create(name="Test Publisher 2", num_awards=3)
+        author2 = Author.objects.create(name="Test Author 2", age=25)
+        author2.save()
+        # Set the author2's age to user's id to create a relationship we can test
+        author_with_user_id = Author.objects.create(name="User Author", age=user.id)
+        book2 = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn="0987654321",
+            name="Test Book 2",
+            pages=200,
+            rating=3.5,
+            price=15.0,
+            contact=author_with_user_id,
+            publisher=publisher2,
+            pubdate="2023-02-01"
+        )
+        book2.authors.add(author_with_user_id)
+        
+        # Create a nested subquery annotation that references contact's age (which we set to user.id)
+        owner_user = (
+            Book.objects.filter(publisher=OuterRef("pk"))
+            .annotate(owner_user=Subquery(Book.objects.filter(pk=OuterRef("pk")).values("contact__age")))
+            .values("owner_user")
+        )
+        
+        # Use SimpleLazyObject in the filter
+        lazy_user = SimpleLazyObject(lambda: user.id)
+        
+        # This should not raise a TypeError
+        queryset = Publisher.objects.annotate(owner_user=Subquery(owner_user)).filter(
+            owner_user=lazy_user
+        )
+        
+        # Execute the query to ensure it works
+        result = list(queryset)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result[0], publisher2)

+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

+import copy
+from django.forms import CharField, Form
+from django.test import SimpleTestCase
+
+
+class DeepCopyErrorMessagesOtterTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    def test_field_deepcopy_copies_error_messages(self):
+        """
+        Test that __deepcopy__ creates independent copies of error_messages.
+        Modifying error_messages on one field should not affect another field.
+        """
+        # Create a form class with a CharField
+        class TestForm(Form):
+            field1 = CharField(error_messages={'required': 'Original message'})
+        
+        # Instantiate two separate forms (each deepcopies the field)
+        form1 = TestForm()
+        form2 = TestForm()
+        
+        # Modify error_messages on form1's field1
+        form1.fields['field1'].error_messages['required'] = 'Modified message for form1'
+        
+        # form2's field1 error_messages should remain unchanged
+        # This will fail before the fix because both forms share the same error_messages dict
+        self.assertEqual(
+            form2.fields['field1'].error_messages['required'],
+            'Original message',
+            "form2's field error_messages should not be affected by changes to form1's field error_messages"
+        )
+        
+        # Verify form1 has the modified message
+        self.assertEqual(
+            form1.fields['field1'].error_messages['required'],
+            'Modified message for form1'
+        )

+from django.db import models
+from django.db.models import Max
+from django.test import TestCase
+from .models import Author, Book
+
+
+class MetaOrderingGroupByOtterTest(TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpTestData(cls):
+        cls.a1 = Author.objects.create(name='Author 1', age=35)
+        cls.a2 = Author.objects.create(name='Author 2', age=45)
+        cls.a3 = Author.objects.create(name='Author 3', age=57)
+        
+        cls.b1 = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn='1234567890',
+            name='Book 1',
+            pages=100,
+            rating=4.5,
+            price=10.0,
+            contact=cls.a1,
+            publisher=None,
+            pubdate='2020-01-01'
+        )
+        cls.b1.authors.add(cls.a1)
+        
+        cls.b2 = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn='1234567891',
+            name='Book 2',
+            pages=200,
+            rating=3.0,
+            price=20.0,
+            contact=cls.a2,
+            publisher=None,
+            pubdate='2020-01-02'
+        )
+        cls.b2.authors.add(cls.a2)
+        
+        cls.b3 = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn='1234567892',
+            name='Book 3',
+            pages=300,
+            rating=4.0,
+            price=30.0,
+            contact=cls.a3,
+            publisher=None,
+            pubdate='2020-01-03'
+        )
+        cls.b3.authors.add(cls.a3)
+        
+        cls.b4 = Book.objects.create(
+            isbn='1234567893',
+            name='Book 4',
+            pages=400,
+            rating=5.0,
+            price=40.0,
+            contact=cls.a3,
+            publisher=None,
+            pubdate='2020-01-04'
+        )
+        cls.b4.authors.add(cls.a3)
+
+    def test_meta_ordering_not_in_group_by(self):
+        """
+        Test that Meta.ordering fields are not included in GROUP BY clause
+        when performing aggregation with values().
+        
+        This test ensures that when a model has Meta.ordering defined,
+        those ordering fields don't interfere with GROUP BY aggregation.
+        The aggregation should group only by the fields specified in values(),
+        not by Meta.ordering fields.
+        """
+        # Book model has Meta.ordering defined
+        # We group by rating and aggregate max age
+        # Meta.ordering should not affect the GROUP BY clause
+        books = Book.objects.values('rating').annotate(oldest=Max('authors__age')).order_by('rating')
+        
+        # We expect 4 distinct ratings with their corresponding max author ages
+        # If Meta.ordering incorrectly adds fields to GROUP BY, we might get
+        # incorrect aggregation results
+        result = list(books)
+        
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            result,
+            [
+                {'rating': 3.0, 'oldest': 45},
+                {'rating': 4.0, 'oldest': 57},
+                {'rating': 4.5, 'oldest': 35},
+                {'rating': 5.0, 'oldest': 57},
+            ]
+        )

+import numpy as np
+from sklearn.cluster import OPTICS
+from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
+
+
+def test_optics_float_min_samples():
+    """Test that OPTICS works with float min_samples parameter.
+    
+    This test ensures that when min_samples is passed as a float (e.g., 0.1),
+    it is properly converted to an integer before being passed to 
+    NearestNeighbors, which only accepts integer values for n_neighbors.
+    
+    The bug was that min_samples was calculated as a float but not converted
+    to int, causing a TypeError when instantiating NearestNeighbors.
+    """
+    # Create sample data
+    X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=50, centers=3, random_state=42)
+    
+    # This should not raise a TypeError about n_neighbors not accepting float
+    clust = OPTICS(metric='minkowski', n_jobs=-1, min_samples=0.1)
+    clust.fit(X)
+    
+    # Verify that the clustering was performed successfully
+    assert hasattr(clust, 'labels_')
+    assert len(clust.labels_) == len(X)

+import re

+from django.test import RequestFactory, TestCase
+from django.contrib.auth.models import User
+from .models import ProfileCollection, Profile
+
+
+class RegexPrefixOtterTest(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that formset prefixes containing regex special characters
+    don't cause data loss in admin changeform view.
+    """
+    
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpTestData(cls):
+        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(
+            username='super',
+            password='secret',
+            email='super@example.com'
+        )
+    
+    def test_formset_prefix_with_regex_special_characters(self):
+        """
+        Test that a formset prefix containing regex special characters
+        (like parentheses, dots, etc.) doesn't break the pk_pattern matching
+        in ModelAdmin._changeform_view, which could lead to data loss.
+        """
+        # Create a ProfileCollection with a Profile
+        collection = ProfileCollection.objects.create(name='Test Collection')
+        profile = Profile.objects.create(
+            collection=collection,
+            first_name='John',
+            last_name='Doe'
+        )
+        
+        # Create a custom inline with a prefix containing regex special characters
+        class CustomInline(ModelAdmin):
+            model = Profile
+            
+            def get_formsets_with_inlines(self, request, obj=None):
+                # Use a prefix with regex special characters like parentheses and dots
+                from django.forms.models import inlineformset_factory
+                FormSet = inlineformset_factory(
+                    ProfileCollection,
+                    Profile,
+                    fields=['first_name', 'last_name'],
+                    extra=0
+                )
+                # Override the prefix to include regex special characters
+                FormSet.prefix = 'test(prefix).with+special*chars'
+                yield FormSet, self
+        
+        # Create ModelAdmin instance
+        site = AdminSite()

+        
+        # Create a request simulating a POST to save the formset
+        factory = RequestFactory()
+        prefix = 'test(prefix).with+special*chars'
+        
+        # Simulate POST data for updating the existing profile
+        post_data = {

+            f'{prefix}-INITIAL_FORMS': '1',
+            f'{prefix}-MIN_NUM_FORMS': '0',
+            f'{prefix}-MAX_NUM_FORMS': '1000',
+            f'{prefix}-0-id': str(profile.pk),
+            f'{prefix}-0-first_name': 'Jane',
+            f'{prefix}-0-last_name': 'Smith',
+            f'{prefix}-0-collection': str(collection.pk),
+        }
+        
+        request = factory.post(f'/admin/admin_inlines/profilecollection/{collection.pk}/change/', post_data)
+        request.user = self.superuser
+        
+        # Test the pk_pattern regex compilation and matching
+        # This simulates what happens in ModelAdmin._changeform_view

+        
+        # The bug: without re.escape(), special characters in prefix break the regex
+        # This should not raise an exception

+            # Without re.escape(), this would fail or behave incorrectly
+            # Let's verify the buggy version would fail
+            buggy_pattern = re.compile(r'{}-\d+-{}$'.format(prefix, pk_name))
+            # The buggy pattern treats special chars as regex operators
+            # For example, parentheses create capture groups, dots match any character, etc.
+            # This assertion ensures our fix is needed

+from django.test import TestCase
+from django.db.models import Prefetch
+
+from .models import Author, Book
+
+
+class PrefetchSlicedQuerysetOtterTest(TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpTestData(cls):
+        cls.author1 = Author.objects.create(name="Author 1", first_book_id=1)
+        cls.author2 = Author.objects.create(name="Author 2", first_book_id=1)
+        
+        # Create multiple books for each author
+        cls.books_author1 = []
+        for i in range(5):
+            book = Book.objects.create(title=f"Author 1 Book {i}")
+            book.authors.add(cls.author1)
+            cls.books_author1.append(book)
+        
+        cls.books_author2 = []
+        for i in range(5):
+            book = Book.objects.create(title=f"Author 2 Book {i}")
+            book.authors.add(cls.author2)
+            cls.books_author2.append(book)
+
+    def test_prefetch_with_sliced_queryset(self):
+        """
+        Test that Prefetch objects work with sliced querysets.
+        This should prefetch only the first 3 books for each author.
+        """
+        authors = Author.objects.prefetch_related(
+            Prefetch(
+                'books',
+                queryset=Book.objects.all()[:3],
+                to_attr='example_books',
+            )
+        )
+        
+        authors_list = list(authors)
+        
+        # Each author should have exactly 3 books in example_books
+        self.assertEqual(len(authors_list[0].example_books), 3)
+        self.assertEqual(len(authors_list[1].example_books), 3)
+        
+        # Verify the books belong to the correct authors
+        for book in authors_list[0].example_books:
+            self.assertIn(authors_list[0], book.authors.all())
+        for book in authors_list[1].example_books:
+            self.assertIn(authors_list[1], book.authors.all())

+from sympy import S, Lambda, imageset, FiniteSet, I
+from sympy.abc import n
+
+
+def test_imageset_intersect_reals_membership():
+    """Test that membership check in intersection with Reals works correctly.
+    
+    This test addresses the bug where:
+    S1 = imageset(Lambda(n, n + (n - 1)*(n + 1)*I), S.Integers)
+    2 in S1 returns False (correct)
+    but 2 in S1.intersect(Reals) returns True (incorrect, should be False)
+    
+    The correct behavior is that S1.intersect(Reals) should equal {-1, 1},
+    so 2 should not be in the intersection.
+    """
+    S1 = imageset(Lambda(n, n + (n - 1)*(n + 1)*I), S.Integers)
+    
+    # 2 should not be in S1
+    assert 2 not in S1
+    
+    # 2 should not be in S1.intersect(S.Reals) - this is the bug
+    assert 2 not in S1.intersect(S.Reals)
+    
+    # The intersection should be {-1, 1}
+    # When n = -1: -1 + (-2)(0)*I = -1 (real)
+    # When n = 0: 0 + (-1)(1)*I = -I (not real)
+    # When n = 1: 1 + (0)(2)*I = 1 (real)
+    # When n = 2: 2 + (1)(3)*I = 2 + 3I (not real)
+    assert S1.intersect(S.Reals) == FiniteSet(-1, 1)
+    
+    # Additional checks
+    assert -1 in S1.intersect(S.Reals)
+    assert 1 in S1.intersect(S.Reals)
+    assert 0 not in S1.intersect(S.Reals)

+from django.test import RequestFactory, SimpleTestCase
+from django.views.debug import ExceptionReporter
+
+
+class SuppressContextOtterTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    """
+    Test that ExceptionReporter respects __suppress_context__ (PEP 415)
+    when an exception is raised with 'raise ... from None'.
+    """
+
+    def test_suppress_context_with_raise_from_none(self):
+        """
+        When an exception is raised with 'raise ... from None',
+        the __suppress_context__ flag should be respected and the
+        original exception should not appear in the traceback frames.
+        """
+        request = RequestFactory().get('/')
+        
+        try:
+            try:
+                raise RuntimeError('original error')
+            except Exception:
+                raise ValueError('new error') from None
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            reporter = ExceptionReporter(request, ValueError, exc, exc.__traceback__)
+            frames = reporter.get_traceback_frames()
+            
+            # Collect all exception messages from the frames
+            # The frames list contains the exception chain that the reporter found
+            exception_messages = []
+            for frame_data in frames:
+                # Each frame can have exception info
+                pass
+            
+            # Check the actual HTML output which will contain the exceptions
+            html = reporter.get_traceback_html()
+            
+            # When 'raise ... from None' is used, __suppress_context__ is True
+            # and the original RuntimeError should NOT be in the output
+            self.assertIn('new error', html)
+            self.assertNotIn('original error', html)

+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import matplotlib.cm as cm
+from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import warnings
+
+
+def test_colormap_registration_with_different_names():
+    """
+    Test that a colormap can be registered with a name different from its
+    internal name attribute, and that it can be used via pyplot interface
+    with the registered name.
+    
+    This is a regression test for the issue where registering a colormap
+    with a name different from its .name attribute would cause errors when
+    trying to use it with pyplot functions like imshow().
+    """
+    # Create a colormap with one name
+    my_cmap_data = [[1.5e-03, 4.7e-04, 1.4e-02],
+                    [2.3e-03, 1.3e-03, 1.8e-02],
+                    [3.3e-03, 2.3e-03, 2.4e-02]]
+    my_cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list('some_cmap_name', my_cmap_data)
+    
+    # Register it with a different name using the new API
+    # Suppress deprecation warnings if the old API is still present
+    with warnings.catch_warnings():
+        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
+        try:
+            # Try new API first (matplotlib >= 3.5)
+            from matplotlib import colormaps
+            colormaps.register(cmap=my_cmap, name='my_cmap_name')
+        except (ImportError, AttributeError):
+            # Fall back to old API
+            cm.register_cmap(name='my_cmap_name', cmap=my_cmap)
+    
+    try:
+        # Set the colormap using the registered name
+        plt.set_cmap('my_cmap_name')
+        
+        # This should work without raising a ValueError
+        # The issue was that it would look up 'some_cmap_name' instead of 'my_cmap_name'
+        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
+        im = ax.imshow([[1, 1], [2, 2]])
+        
+        # Verify that the colormap is correctly set
+        assert im.get_cmap().name == 'my_cmap_name'
+        
+        plt.close(fig)
+    finally:
+        # Clean up: unregister the colormap
+        with warnings.catch_warnings():
+            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
+            try:
+                from matplotlib import colormaps
+                colormaps.unregister('my_cmap_name')
+            except (ImportError, AttributeError):
+                cm.unregister_cmap('my_cmap_name')

+import os
+import sys
+from django.core.management import call_command
+from django.test import override_settings
+from .test_base import MigrationTestBase
+
+
+class MakeMigrationsCheckNoWriteOtterTest(MigrationTestBase):
+    """
+    Test that makemigrations --check does not write migration files.
+    This ensures consistency with other --check commands like migrate --check
+    and optimizemigration --check.
+    """
+
+    def test_makemigrations_check_does_not_write_files(self):
+        """
+        Test that makemigrations --check exits without writing migration files
+        when there are changes detected.
+        """
+        # Use temporary_migration_module to create a scenario with pending migrations
+        with self.temporary_migration_module(module="migrations.test_migrations") as migration_dir:
+            # Add a new model to trigger migration creation
+            from django.apps import apps
+            from django.db import models
+            
+            # Get the models module for the migrations app
+            app_config = apps.get_app_config('migrations')
+            
+            # Create a new model class dynamically
+            new_model = type(
+                'NewTestModel',
+                (models.Model,),
+                {
+                    '__module__': 'migrations.models',
+                    'test_field': models.CharField(max_length=100),
+                    'Meta': type('Meta', (), {'app_label': 'migrations'}),
+                }
+            )
+            
+            # Register the model
+            app_config.models['newtestmodel'] = new_model
+            
+            try:
+                # Count files before running makemigrations --check
+                initial_files = set(os.listdir(migration_dir))
+                
+                # Run makemigrations --check
+                # This should detect changes and exit with code 1, but NOT write files
+                try:
+                    call_command(
+                        "makemigrations",
+                        "migrations",
+                        "--check",
+                        verbosity=0,
+                    )
+                    changes_detected = False
+                except SystemExit as e:
+                    changes_detected = (e.code == 1)
+                
+                # Count files after running makemigrations --check
+                final_files = set(os.listdir(migration_dir))
+                new_files = final_files - initial_files
+                
+                # Filter out non-migration files
+                new_migration_files = [
+                    f for f in new_files 
+                    if f.endswith('.py') and f != '__init__.py' and not f.startswith('__pycache__')
+                ]
+                
+                # The test should fail on old code (files are written) and pass on new code (no files written)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    len(new_migration_files), 
+                    0,
+                    f"makemigrations --check should not write migration files, "
+                    f"but found: {new_migration_files}"
+                )
+            finally:
+                # Clean up the dynamically created model
+                if 'newtestmodel' in app_config.models:
+                    del app_config.models['newtestmodel']

+from io import BytesIO

+from django.core.handlers.wsgi import WSGIHandler
+from django.http import HttpResponse
+from django.test import RequestFactory, SimpleTestCase, override_settings
+
+
+class HeadRequestOtterTest(SimpleTestCase):
+    """
+    Test that runserver (WSGIHandler) strips response body for HEAD requests.
+    """
+
+    def test_head_request_strips_body(self):
+        """
+        WSGIHandler should return empty body for HEAD requests to comply with
+        RFC 2616, section 4.3.
+        """
+        # Create a simple view that returns content
+        def test_view(request):
+            return HttpResponse(b"This content should not appear in HEAD response")
+
+        # Create a HEAD request
+        factory = RequestFactory()
+        request_environ = factory.head('/').environ
+
+        # Mock start_response to capture what's being sent
+        response_status = []
+        response_headers = []
+
+        def start_response(status, headers):
+            response_status.append(status)
+            response_headers.append(headers)
+
+        # Create WSGIHandler and process the request
+        handler = WSGIHandler()
+        
+        # Override get_response to use our test view
+        original_get_response = handler.get_response
+        
+        def mock_get_response(request):
+            return test_view(request)
+        
+        handler.get_response = mock_get_response
+        
+        # Call the handler
+        response = handler(request_environ, start_response)
+        
+        # Collect the response body
+        response_body = b''.join(response)
+        
+        # The response body should be empty for HEAD requests
+        self.assertEqual(
+            response_body,
+            b'',
+            "HEAD request should return empty body, but got: %r" % response_body
+        )

+from django.db import models

+from django.test import TestCase
+
+
+class Thing(models.Model):
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'aggregation'
+
+
+class Related(models.Model):
+    thing = models.ForeignKey(Thing, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
+    
+    class Meta:
+        app_label = 'aggregation'
+
+
+class RandomOrderingAggregationOtterTest(TestCase):
+    """
+    Test that order_by('?') does not break queryset aggregation.
+    """
+    
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        super().setUpClass()
+        # Create tables for our test models
+        from django.db import connection
+        with connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
+            schema_editor.create_model(Thing)
+            schema_editor.create_model(Related)
+    
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        # Clean up tables
+        from django.db import connection
+        with connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
+            schema_editor.delete_model(Related)
+            schema_editor.delete_model(Thing)
+        super().tearDownClass()
+    
+    def test_random_ordering_does_not_break_aggregation(self):
+        """
+        Test that using order_by('?') with Count aggregation produces
+        correct grouped results, not broken down results.

+        Related.objects.create(thing=t)

+                        "Count should be 2 for the single Thing with 2 Related objects")

+    when plotting less than 12 months and January is not included.

+    This is a regression test for the bug where the year doesn't show
+    anywhere when plotting < 1 year without January in the x-axis.

+

+    
+    # Get the offset string

+
